question: Ploché krabice, ve kterých si z IKEA vozíme nábytek, prý vymyslel jeden zaměstnanec, když si nevěděl rady se stolem. Ten stůl se mu totiž nevešel… kam?
source_excerpt: Gillis Lundgren, a young IKEA designer, couldn't fit a table into his car and removed its legs

extra.why_interesting: Players assume flat-pack was a deliberate engineering or cost strategy. It actually began with a man struggling to load a table into a car, which fits a car-trip audience perfectly. It is easy to reason out from the stem.
extra.verification_notes: Popular accounts consistently say Gillis Lundgren could not fit a table into his car and removed its legs, which led to flat-pack furniture (https://www.dezeen.com/2013/07/22/ikea-revives-three-legged-diy-side-table/). I did not read the Dezeen page itself, only the search summary.

explanation: Gillis Lundgren tehdy stolu prostě odšrouboval nohy, aby ho dostal do auta. Z té nouzovky se stal princip, na kterém IKEA stojí dodnes.

question: Zakladatel IKEA Ingvar Kamprad dal výrobkům místo číselných kódů jména, protože se mu čísla při čtení pletla. Jakou poruchu, kterou zná snad každá česká škola, měl?

extra.why_interesting: Everyone has puzzled over names like BILLY or KLIPPAN without asking why IKEA uses names at all. The answer is a personal reason that Czechs know from school, and the naming system in the explanation adds a second surprise.
extra.verification_notes: Kamprad described himself as dyslexic and said he used names because numbers were hard to remember, per https://dyslexiahelp.umich.edu/success-story/ingvar-kamprad/.

explanation: Jména si pamatoval mnohem snáz než čísla, a tak vznikl celý systém. Pohovky nesou jména švédských míst, postele norských a koberce dánských.
